title: A Tradition of Their Own
title_ja: 二人でつくる新しい習慣
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の人物、組織、法律、調査結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: When two people decide to share their lives, they may discover that activities which appear ordinary to one person have a particular significance for the other.
sentences.ja: 二人が生活を共にすると決めると、一人には普通に思える活動がもう一人には特別な意味を持つと気づくことがある。

sentences.en: A familiar routine may have developed in response to the circumstances of a person's family, even if that person has rarely considered the reasons for it.
sentences.ja: 身近な習慣は本人が理由をほとんど考えたことがなくても家族の事情に応じて発展した場合がある。

sentences.en: Differences in such routines do not necessarily indicate a disagreement about the values that the people involved consider important.
sentences.ja: 習慣の違いは関係者が重要と考える価値観の不一致を必ずしも示さない。

sentences.en: Sometimes a conversation about the origin of a routine can reveal an unexpected similarity between two apparently different practices.
sentences.ja: 時に習慣の由来についての会話が一見異なる二つの慣行の予想外の類似性を明らかにし得る。

sentences.en: Consider a fictional couple who are discussing how to spend the first weekend of each month.
sentences.ja: 毎月最初の週末の過ごし方を話し合っている架空の二人を考えよう。

sentences.en: One person hopes to organize a meal with relatives because regular gatherings were an important feature of their childhood.
sentences.ja: 一人は定期的な集まりが幼少期の重要な特徴だったので親族との食事を企画したいと思う。

sentences.en: The other prefers to spend that weekend quietly at home, having grown up in a family that treated free time as an opportunity to rest after a busy week.
sentences.ja: もう一人は自由時間を忙しい一週間の後に休む機会と考える家庭で育ったので、その週末は家で静かに過ごす方を好む。

sentences.en: At first, each interprets the other's proposal as a rejection of something that they personally value.
sentences.ja: 当初、それぞれは相手の提案を自分が大切にするものの拒絶と解釈する。

sentences.en: They decide to explain what they find especially meaningful about their familiar routines.
sentences.ja: 身近な習慣の何を特に意味あると感じるか説明することにする。

sentences.en: The first person describes the importance of maintaining relationships with relatives, while the second explains the value of having predictable opportunities to recover from everyday responsibilities.
sentences.ja: 一人は親族との関係維持の重要性を説明し、もう一人は日常の責任から回復する予測可能な機会の価値を説明する。

sentences.en: Both recognize that these purposes might be achieved through arrangements other than the ones they had originally proposed.
sentences.ja: 双方はこうした目的が当初提案した以外の仕組みによっても達成され得ると認識する。

sentences.en: They begin discussing the frequency and form of family gatherings rather than treating the entire tradition as something that must either be accepted or rejected.
sentences.ja: 伝統全体を受容か拒絶のどちらかと扱わず集まりの頻度や形態を議論し始める。

sentences.en: The couple eventually proposes an arrangement that includes both planned visits and protected periods of personal time.
sentences.ja: 二人は最終的に計画された訪問と確保された個人時間の両方を含む仕組みを提案する。

sentences.en: They agree to review the plan when their responsibilities or circumstances change.
sentences.ja: 責任や事情が変化したら計画を見直すと合意する。

sentences.en: Their fictional conversation does not establish a practical solution that would be appropriate for every relationship.
sentences.ja: 架空会話は全ての関係に適した実用的解決策を確立しない。

sentences.en: Instead, it illustrates the difference between preserving a particular routine and protecting the purpose that the routine was intended to serve.
sentences.ja: 代わりに特定習慣の維持とその習慣が果たす目的の保護との違いを例示する。

sentences.en: Shared traditions do not always need to be inherited in their original form.
sentences.ja: 共有する伝統は常に元の形で継承される必要はない。

sentences.en: People can sometimes create new practices that reflect values they have learned to recognize in one another.
sentences.ja: 人は互いに認識できるようになった価値観を反映する新しい慣行を作れることがある。

sentences.en: Understanding the purpose of a familiar practice can provide a starting point for such a process.
sentences.ja: 身近な慣行の目的を理解することはそうした過程の出発点になり得る。

sentences.en: The resulting tradition may become meaningful precisely because both people participated in shaping it.
sentences.ja: 生まれた伝統はまさに二人が形作ることに参加したため意味あるものになり得る。

vocabulary.definition: in a way that must occur
things one is expected to do

questions.prompt: Why might differences in routines not mean differences in values?
options: Every person has exactly the same routines.
Similar values can be expressed through different practices.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる行動でも価値観が近いことがある。

questions.prompt: What may a routine develop in response to?
options: Only the age of the person.
The circumstances of a person's family.
A universal rule for every household.

questions.prompt: What does the first person hope to organize?
Why does the second person prefer a quiet weekend?
options: They value rest after everyday responsibilities.
They want to reject all relationships.

questions.prompt: What do the couple begin discussing?
options: Which person is required to abandon every value.
The cost of a new home alone.
The frequency and form of gatherings.

questions.prompt: Why explain the purposes of their routines?
options: It proves that both routines must be unchanged forever.
It reveals that the values might be respected through alternative arrangements.
It guarantees that no disagreement will arise.
It makes the other's preference irrelevant.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的を別の方法で満たす可能性。

questions.prompt: What does their proposed arrangement include?
options: Planned visits and protected personal time.

questions.prompt: Why agree to review the arrangement?
options: The original plan cannot be useful.
The fictional discussion proves all arrangements identical.
One person's original routine must always replace the other's.
A meaningful tradition cannot be changed.
All disagreements about routines reflect opposite values.
Shared traditions can develop through understanding the purposes behind different practices.
questions.explanation_ja: 目的を理解して共同の習慣をつくる。

paraphrases.source: A familiar routine may have developed in response to the circumstances of a person's family, even if that person has rarely considered the reasons for it.
paraphrases.rewrite: Routines may arise from family circumstances even without conscious reflection.

paraphrases.source: The other prefers to spend that weekend quietly at home, having grown up in a family that treated free time as an opportunity to rest after a busy week.
paraphrases.rewrite: Their preference for rest reflects the way free time was valued in their family.

paraphrases.source: They begin discussing the frequency and form of family gatherings rather than treating the entire tradition as something that must either be accepted or rejected.
paraphrases.rewrite: They examine possible forms of gatherings instead of seeing tradition as an all-or-nothing choice.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 二択から具体的調整へ。

paraphrases.source: The resulting tradition may become meaningful precisely because both people participated in shaping it.
paraphrases.rewrite: The new tradition can matter because both partners helped create it.
